answer: Sybil resistance requires each identity to complete a prescribed sequence of modular squarings, with each result feeding the next and preventing useful parallelization within that computation. GPUs can run separate chains, but cannot reduce one identity’s elapsed delay; creating clones therefore multiplies hardware and energy costs rather than bypassing the time lock. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify completion efficiently for glacier sensors, nebula observatories, or harbor relays.
